newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Big buyer boosts UCB and underpins Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Big buyer boosts UCB and underpins Brussels bourse.

text.p: An aggressive and anonymous buyer snapped up all shares offered in chemicals and drugs firm UCB on Tuesday, boosting the price to new highs and underpinning an otherwise flat bourse, traders said.

"The feature of the day is UCB," one trader said. "It is obvious that something is going on. There is one buyer who is taking everything, but he is not showing himself. Sure the results will be good, but it is obvious that this buying is not simply for financial interests," he added.
The share was up 3.03 percent at a 1997 high of 139,300 francs at 0910 GMT.
Generale Bank said in its market commentary that despite UCB's rally of more than 60 percent this year its price/earnings ratio remained in line with its sector.

"We see the continued appetite for pharmaceuticals all over Europe and the release of UCB's H1 results on July 30, which as usual might be even better than hinted at by UCB, as major drivers behind the ongoing share price rally," the bank said.
Elsewhere on the generally directionless market electronics firm Barco provided some upside relief, rising 0.9 percent to a 1997 high of 7,680 francs.

Traders said the new rise of one of the market's favourite growth stocks was due to a favourable appreciation of the company's announcement late on Friday of its purchase of Danish audio and video firm RE.
SGB was off 80 francs at 3,570 after rising strongly last week on a flush of optimism after it nearly halved its stake in non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere to just 25 percent.
Retailer Colruyt continued Monday's decline, dropping 1.96 percent to 18,750 francs on a technical reaction to its recent rally.
The Bel-20 index of blue-chip shares was 1.18 points or 0.05 percent higher at 2,502.50, having moved in a 2,503.52/2,494.88 range.
There were 11 losers, three unchanged and six gainers.
